transcript: Yesterday, I went to The Blood Quilt by Katori Hall at Lincoln Center. This is a play about four half-sisters convening at the home they grew up in on an island off the state of Georgia. It's the first week of May, so they have their long standing annual quilt making tradition to take care of, but with their mother having just passed away, there are other things to address as well. Wounds are reopened, secrets revealed, and plenty of good old familial resentment crops up. I thought there were some far fetched plot points here and there, and some moments of stiff or meandering writing, but otherwise I thought this was pretty solid. The characters are well-defined and well-motivated, their relationships believable, and the premise, though familiar, was very intriguing. The Blood Quilt is running at Lincoln Center through the end of the year. With that, another playbill for my collection.
